name: Misra–Gries bounded frequent-item counters
definition: Maintain at most k−1 positive counters c_i; for an existing item i set c_i←c_i+1, for an untracked item with space set c_i←1, otherwise set every stored c_j←c_j−1 and remove zeros. With N stream items and absent counters interpreted as zero, f_i>N/k implies c_i>0.
variables: k threshold denominator; c_i residual counter for item i (zero when absent); f_i true frequency; N stream length
assumptions: Finite equality-comparable stream, integer k≥2; full review pending
limitations: Residual counts underestimate frequencies; verify exact frequencies on replay; full review pending
computation: Generalize unequal cancellation to k distinct items; verify invariant and error bound before admission.

source.citation: Provisional locator: Misra and Gries (1982), Finding repeated elements, Science of Computer Programming 2(2), 143–152. DOI 10.1016/0167-6423(82)90012-0; full review pending.

application: General categorical stream frequency screening; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Stream, capacity and replay if exact frequencies required.
incompatible_methods: Treating residual counts as exact frequencies
mechanism_note: Provisional generalization of majority cancellation to multiple counters.
